Glossary

The vocabulary, with the distinctions that actually matter - memory vs note vs finding, briefing vs recall, archive vs supersede vs delete.

On this page
  • A–Z
  • Four distinctions worth getting right

Terms are listed alphabetically. The ones worth reading even if you think you know them are the four disambiguation entries at the end: each is a pair people routinely use interchangeably, and each pair means genuinely different things.

A–Z

Agent process - the claude or codex process that runs an agent's hooks and launches its MCP transports. The SessionStart hook stamps its identity on the ambient session, and the agent's MCP requests name it, which binds the agent's tool calls to that session with no session_start. See Sessions & briefings.

Ambient session - a Seamless session opened automatically by a Claude Code or Codex SessionStart hook, without the agent asking, displayed with an opaque cc/... or cx/... handle. Lifecycle identity uses the full external session ID plus client, not the display handle. Contrast explicit session.

Approver - a credential that signs your approval of an agent's access to a locked project: a passkey, or on a Mac a Touch ID key kept by the Seamless Approve app. Each is enrolled once, with a one-time code only the daemon's account can mint. None is required: seam approve in your own terminal approves with sudo as the proof. See Enroll an approver.

Archive - marking a Seamless memory invalid because it is no longer relevant: it leaves the indexes and stays readable. The gardener's staleness pass proposes it, and never for a constraint or a pinned stage.

Backup - one archive of a whole Seamless instance, of the kind seamlessd export writes: every memory and note, a snapshot of the database, and a list of what each project holds. A release install takes one every day and keeps the newest 7 in ~/.seamless/backups; Settings > Backups in the console lists and restores them. See Import, back up & restore.

Binding - the association between an MCP connection and a Seamless session, set by session_start or, for a Claude Code or Codex agent, automatically through its agent process; an explicit session_start wins. Everything on that connection inherits the bound session's project.

Briefing - the <seam-briefing> context block Seamless injects into an agent at session start - constraints, pinned stages, plan rollups, the memory index, recent findings - assembled inside a token budget. See Sessions & briefings.

Claim - an atomic, leased hold on a Seamless task, taken with tasks_claim; exactly one agent can hold a live claim.

Client - in a networked Seamless setup, a computer whose agents use the Server's daemon and data. It runs no daemon and keeps no data of its own, and reaches the Server through a relay or with a key. See Networked Seamless.

Confidential - the isolation state in which nothing leaves a Seamless project: sessions bound elsewhere cannot read it, and its own sessions cannot write outside it. Its agents still read global memories and open projects.

Console - Seamless's read-mostly web UI at /console, an observability surface for the human owner; agents use MCP.

Constraint - the Seamless memory kind for a rule the project cannot violate; pinned into every briefing, never dropped for budget, never staleness-archived.

Description - the one-line summary in a Seamless memory's frontmatter, the only text shown in any index and therefore the entire retrieval surface. See Write memories that get recalled.

Digest - a note summarizing a Seamless project's recent activity, proposed by the gardener.

Explicit session - a Seamless session opened by calling session_start. Without a name, the call adopts the calling agent's existing ambient session rather than opening a second one; a Claude Code or Codex agent that names a different project gets a separate session there instead.

Family - a set of Seamless projects related by parent/child, so a child's briefing can carry the parent's memories and a sibling's recent findings.

Fail closed - the Seamless rule that a durable write with no resolvable scope is rejected rather than defaulted to global. See Projects & scope.

Fail open - the Seamless rule that a hook never blocks an agent: an internal error still returns success. The cost is that failure is silent.

Finding - what a Seamless session learned, passed to session_end and surfaced in later briefings. Not a memory: a finding is what happened, a memory is what is true.

FTS5 - SQLite's built-in full-text search engine, the keyword half of Seamless recall.

Gardener - the Seamless background pass that finds duplicates, staleness, and drift and proposes fixes; it never acts on its own. See The gardener.

Gate - what a Seamless task waits on outside Seamless: who must act and what must happen. A step whose own gate is open, or that a gate task (kind: gate) blocks, is not ready; a person's action clears it. See Tasks & plans.

Global - the Seamless scope with no project, visible to every agent in every repo. A write lands there when it passes project: global, or when it comes from a session bound to the global scope: a session_start with neither project nor cwd, or a session started outside any git repo. A write with no scope at all is refused rather than defaulted here (see fail closed).

Held write - an agent write that write screening kept out of the corpus: one that failed a screen, a change to a binding rule from a session that read outside text, or a supersede, delete or demotion of a constraint. It waits in a queue in the database, never under memory/ or notes/, until you release or discard it on the console's Held screen. The agent is told it is held.

Isolation - a Seamless project's fence: open (the default), confidential (nothing leaves) or sealed (nothing enters or leaves). It governs what flows in and out of a project; whether even its own agents need your approval first is the separate locked project setting. See Project isolation.

Kind - a Seamless memory's type: constraint, convention, runbook, protocol, gotcha, decision, refuted, reference, or stage. See Memory & notes.

Lab - a shared Seamless workspace for a systematic investigation, holding trials; opened with lab_open.

Lease - a time limit on something held in Seamless. A task claim's lease (default 900 seconds) and a repo lock's are refreshed by claiming or acquiring again, and once one runs out the task or lock is free to take, so a crashed agent strands nothing. Under peer_auth, your approval of an agent's access to a locked project is a lease too: it covers that agent's process tree until it expires, its session ends or you revoke it, and nothing extends it. See Lease-based task claiming and Leases and the process tree.

Locked project - a Seamless project that stays closed to every agent of yours until you approve one agent's access, for a limited time, with a proof the agent cannot produce: Touch ID, a passkey, or your own sudo. It needs peer_auth and is also confidential or sealed. You lock one from its Overview with a passkey, or force it in the config file (peer_auth.force_locked). See Lock projects behind your approval.

Memory - in Seamless, a markdown file with YAML frontmatter holding one durable piece of knowledge; the unit that reaches briefings.

Note - in Seamless, a markdown file holding a work artifact - research findings, a meeting summary, a design record; found via recall, never injected into a briefing.

Open - the default isolation state: the project shares normally, global knowledge flows in, and family surfaces may include it.

Owner signature - the second signature on a Seamless release, checksums.txt.sshsig, made by the owner with a hardware security key before the release is published. The installers check it on every release that has one; the updater checks it only when update.release_signers pins the owner's keys. See Owner-signed releases.

Pairing - how a Client gets a credential of its own from the Server: a one-time code from the console's Devices page (or seamlessd devices code), after which the computer holds a key, or for a relay a TLS client certificate, that you can revoke. Under peer_auth the code alone pairs nothing until you approve the computer with a passkey. See Pairing.

peer_auth - the optional Seamless deployment in which the daemon runs as an OS account of its own and names each caller by the uid the kernel reports for its Unix-socket connection, never by anything the caller sends. Locked projects and restricted local accounts rest on it. macOS and Linux only, and off by default. See Lock projects behind your approval.

Plan - in Seamless, not a primitive but a composition keyed by plan:<slug>: a narrative note, supporting notes, and step tasks. See Tasks & plans.

Project - the scope a Seamless memory, note, task, or session belongs to; resolved from an explicit argument, a bound session, or the agent's cwd.

Proposal - the Seamless gardener's output: a suggestion for the owner to review, applied only when someone decides to, with gardener_apply or from the console's Gardener inbox.

Provenance - the Seamless record of where knowledge came from and what replaced it: source_session, superseded_by, invalid_at.

Ready - a Seamless task with no unfinished blocker and no open gate; tasks_ready returns exactly those.

Recall - Seamless's single search entry point, fusing FTS5 keyword matching and vector similarity with RRF. Also, loosely, the <seam-recall> block injected on prompt match - see the disambiguation below.

Relay - the small daemon on a macOS or Linux Client, run by an account of its own, that serves the local socket its agents dial and forwards each request to the Server over TLS with its own client certificate, carrying the caller's uid and process chain. A computer with a relay holds no bearer key. See The relay.

Repo lock - a Seamless lock on a repository's refs (its main branch, or a tag pattern), declared once per repository and name and held with a lease by one session while it lands changes. It belongs to the repository, never to a project, and is always named with it: LOCK seamless main. Sessions waiting for a busy one queue for it and take it first come, first served (seam lock acquire --wait). An optional feature, off by default.

Reproject - moving a Seamless memory to a different project that already exists; moving it to one that does not is a split.

Restricted local account - a second OS account whose agents work beside yours under peer_auth, listed in peer_auth.restricted. It reaches every open project that is not locked, reads the global scope without writing it, and everything it writes is labeled with its name. The console's Privacy screen calls it a "Restricted agent account". See Restricted local accounts.

RRF (reciprocal rank fusion) - the method Seamless recall uses to combine the keyword and vector rankings so neither retriever gets a veto.

Sealed - the isolation state in which nothing enters or leaves a Seamless project: confidential plus no global memories, no family, and no cross-project reads in either direction. Its agents are told the mode in their briefing.

Server - in a networked Seamless setup, the one computer that runs the daemon and keeps the data for every computer; its Clients reach it over the network. macOS or Linux, never Windows. See Networked Seamless.

Session - one agent's stretch of work in Seamless. Sessions heartbeat; an idle one is reaped and marked expired.

Split - dividing one Seamless project into new child projects, creating them and a shared parent; planned as a unit by gardener_split.

Stage - the Seamless memory kind recording where multi-session work stands. It is pinned into briefings while its Status: header names a live gate (open, in_progress or blocked); done unpins it, and a stage with no readable header leaves the briefing after a grace window. See Memory & notes.

Standalone - the default Seamless setup: the daemon, the data and the agents that use them, all on one computer. Contrast Server and Client.

Supersede - replacing an outdated Seamless memory with a new one: the old is marked invalid, leaves the indexes, and stays readable pointing at its replacement.

Trial - one attempt recorded in a Seamless lab: what was tried, what was expected, what happened.

ULID - the id format Seamless uses everywhere, sortable by creation time. Never UUID.

Write screening - the optional Seamless feature that screens every agent write to a memory or note for secrets, injection markers, hidden characters, encoded blobs and unlisted links, and keeps the suspicious ones as held writes for you to release. Off by default. See Screen writes and hold the suspicious ones.

Four distinctions worth getting right

Memory vs. note vs. finding. A memory is what is true (injected into briefings). A note is what you produced (found by searching). A finding is what a session learned (surfaced as recent activity). The test for the first two: would a future agent need this injected before it starts? Then it is a memory.

Briefing vs. recall injection vs. recall call. All three end with the agent knowing something, which is why they blur. The briefing fires at session start and is unconditional. A recall injection fires on prompt match, mid-turn, still without the agent asking. A recall call is the agent choosing to search. The first two are ambient; only the third is a decision. See Recall.

Ambient vs. explicit session. Ambient is opened by the hook, per agent, automatically, and the agent's tool calls are bound to it without asking. Explicit is session_start, which adopts the agent's own ambient session rather than creating a rival - so a Claude Code or Codex agent needs it only to move to another project or resume a named session.

Archive vs. supersede vs. delete. Archive: no longer relevant, marked invalid, still readable. Supersede: replaced by something specific, marked invalid, still readable, pointing at its replacement. Delete: gone. The rule of thumb - delete is for things that were never true; supersede is for things that stopped being true; archive is for things that stopped mattering.
